dialogue:
A: So, have you been keeping up with the World Baseball Classic? I mean, especially the Taiwan games?

B: Oh, totally! I was actually just checking the latest results, and can you believe it? Chinese Taipei managed to beat Korea 5-4 in ten innings!

A: Wait, what? That’s huge! I mean, after those two shutout losses they had at the start, I didn’t think they had it in them.

B: Right? It was a nail-biter! Yu Chang kicked things off with a solo homer, and the crowd in Tokyo Dome was absolutely electric!

A: Oh man, I can just picture it! And then Korea took the lead for a bit, right? What happened there?

B: Exactly! Do Yeong Kim hit a two-run homer that had everyone on the edge of their seats. But then, just when you thought Korea had it, Stuart Fairchild turned it around with a two-run shot of his own.

A: That’s baseball for you! Just when you think you’ve got the game figured out, it flips on you. What a rollercoaster!

B: And let’s not forget Ruei-Yang Gu Lin’s performance. He pitched pretty well, allowing just two hits in his time on the mound. Gotta give credit where it’s due!

A: Absolutely! It’s always fascinating to see these underdog stories unfold. So, what does this mean for their chances moving forward?

B: Well, they’re in a bit of a waiting game now. They need to keep an eye on Australia’s games against Japan and Korea. If the results go their way, they could still sneak into the quarterfinals!

A: Oh wow, that’s so tense! I mean, the pressure must be on for both Taiwan and Korea, right?

B: For sure! It’s like the classic sports drama—one team’s hopes hinge on another team’s performance. Makes you appreciate every pitch!

A: I love that! You know, it’s moments like these that make the WBC so thrilling. It’s not just about the big names; it’s about the heart and hustle of teams like Chinese Taipei.

B: Exactly! And you know, it’s also a reminder of how important international tournaments are for growing the sport globally. 

A: Totally! And speaking of growing the sport, I’m curious—do you think we’ll see more of these surprise victories as the tournament progresses?

B: Oh, definitely! With so many talented players and unpredictable matchups, anything can happen. That’s the beauty of baseball, right?

A: Right! Can’t wait to see how this unfolds. Who knows, maybe Chinese Taipei will make a historic run!

SOURCE TITLE: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Chinese Taipei Defeats Korea 5-4 in ...
SOURCE CONTENT: Chinese Taipei threw a wrench into Pool C of the World Baseball Classic on Sunday afternoon, edging Korea 5-4 in ten innings behind a strong start from Ruei-Yang Gu Lin and timely hitting.
Following two shutout losses to open the tournament, Chinese Taipei rebounded with two crucial wins and must await the results of Australia vs. Japan and Australia vs. Korea to determine whether they can advance to the quarterfinals via a second-place tiebreaker.
With Chinese Taipei’s win, Japan officially clinched a spot in the quarterfinals. Korea will face Australia tomorrow night. Australia controls its own destiny, but if it loses to Japan tonight, Korea’s hopes will remain alive. In that case, Korea would need a win to potentially advance through a tiebreaker.
Yu Chang opened the scoring with a solo home run off Hyun Jin Ryu in the second inning, igniting the packed Taiwanese crowd at the Tokyo Dome.
Korea chased Gu Lin from the game in the fifth and tied it when Shay Whitcomb bounced into a double play that brought home Hyun Min Ahn.
Tsung-Che Cheng put Chinese Taipei back in front in the sixth with a solo shot, but Do Yeong Kim answered with a towering two-run home run to left field off Wei-En Lin to give Korea its first lead of the day.
Gu Lin pitched admirably for Chinese Taipei, allowing just two hits and one run while working into the fifth inning on 59 pitches. Lin then added 2 ⅓ innings in relief, striking out four while allowing two runs.
Ryu went three innings for Korea, throwing 50 pitches and allowing one run on three hits with three strikeouts. Gwak Been followed with 3 ⅓ innings, giving up one run on two hits while striking out three.
In the seventh, Chinese Taipei put the tying run on second and the go-ahead run on first, but Dane Dunning entered and immediately induced a double play to end the threat.
With two outs in the eighth, the game flipped again when Stuart Fairchild hit an opposite-field two-run homer off Dunning to give Chinese Taipei a 4-3 lead.
